title: Leftover wine
subtitle: Making an open bottle last
objectives: Explain what happens to an open bottle
Know how long each style lasts once open

steps.title: Air is the enemy
steps.body: Once opened, wine meets oxygen. At first that can help, but over days it flattens fruit and turns the wine dull, nutty or vinegary. Bacteria can turn alcohol into acetic acid, the acid of vinegar. Cold slows all of this, so the fridge is the best place for any open bottle, red included.

steps.title: How long each lasts
steps.body: Light whites and rosés usually stay pleasant for 2 to 3 days in the fridge with the cork back in. Reds, 3 to 5 days, because tannin protects them. Sparkling wine keeps its fizz for 1 to 3 days with a proper stopper. Fortified wines last longest: an opened tawny Port or Madeira can keep for weeks, Madeira for months.

steps.prompt: Which opened wine is likely to keep longest?
steps.explanation: Madeira has already been exposed to heat and oxygen in its making, and its high acidity and alcohol protect it. It can last months once opened.

steps.body: Pour leftovers into a smaller bottle so there's less air above the wine. Less air, slower decline. The spoon in the neck of a sparkling bottle is a myth; a hinged stopper works.

steps.prompt: Leftover red wine keeps longer if stored in the ____.
steps.explanation: Cold slows oxidation and bacteria. Take a red out half an hour before serving.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Oxygen slowly flattens an open wine
Keep open bottles closed and in the fridge, reds included
Fortified wines last longest; light whites and sparkling the least
